costScope: Entire100000ordinary recipient gift. Allocation60000physical,15000otherpolicy,15000survivor,10000shared/reserve is judgment; physical allocation includes supporting costs. Public construction resources separately stress-tested; no restricted-donation denominator.
geographicAttribution: California benefit fraction .98central,.99favorable,.9adverse is judgment. IncludesSF+restCalifornia residents; excludes out-of-state visitors. No automatic statewide policy spillover and no duplication with SF/Bay edition donations.
formula: Historical diagnostic only, not an expected donor return: qF=sum(k=1..TF)uF*exp(-hazard*(k-.5))/(1+r)^k. qS=sum(k=1..TS)uS/(1+r)^k. V=sum(t=start..start+delay-1)(1+r)^(-t). Qgross=p*b*V*(F*eF*qF+S*eS*qS). Qall=Qgross-H_CA; QCA=gCA*Qgross-H_CA, where harms are modeled in California. Price10=10*G/QCA only for a calibrated positive QCA. Ctiming=G+p*[K*((1+r)^(-(start-1))-(1+r)^(-(start+delay-1)))+M*V]. Cgross=G+p*K/(1+r)^(start-1)+p*M*V.
counterfactual: Same physical package implemented later by public agency/coalition baseline. p jointly includes donor replacement and unique influence; no additional arbitrary attribution multiplier. Only acceleration window counts. Existing cameras/capital not newly purchased by gift.
attribution: Risk share on disjoint package streets, not share of street length. Separate fatal/nonfatal injury categories; reduce intervention priors for transfer/displacement and subtract independent donor harms. No add-on for overlapping survivor distress, physical activity, emissions or other advocates' projects.
uncertainty: All influence, targeting, effect-transfer, utility, duration, geography and cost inputs are judgments.Observed25fatalities and historicalseverecontext do not establish future package risk. Scenarios illustrate sensitivity, not statistical bounds; no verified project.
nativeOutcomes: Additional early exposure-years to a physical traffic-calming package; Incremental fatal and severe nonfatal casualties avoided on disjoint streets; Finite survival and nonfatal impairment QALYs amongCalifornia residents.
